speed.evidence: Measured 2026-09-26 (H07.3) by the H04.3 committee method: GPS epochs with satellites >= 7, HDOP <= 2, speed >= 20 km/h, paired with the 0x2D1 frame nearest in acquisition time (within 20 ms), steady only (|slope of 0x2D1 speed over +/-2 s| < 0.05 g). Per-session median 0x2D1/GPS: 0.9314 (2026-09-20T152758, n=1145), 0.9320 (2026-09-20T175050, n=7521), 0.9348 (2026-09-21T143331, n=910), 0.9324 (_capture-tuning-2026-09-22T235224, n=1010); 10th-90th percentile per epoch about +/-2.5 %. Control on the same epochs: 0x6F7_A reads 0.9236 / 0.9214 / 0.9241 / 0.9233, reproducing the committee's 0.921-0.924, so 0x2D1 reads ~1 % higher than the other ECU copies and does NOT share their 0.9203. The 2026-09-23T150658 HAT drive gave n=119 with a 0.10-1.53 per-epoch spread and is excluded (GNSS integration day). Pre-HAT USB receiver.
The committee relation in committees.yaml (SPEED_SOURCE_DIVERGENCE), which carries the measurements; kept equal to it.

The committee relation in committees.yaml (SPEED_SOURCE_DIVERGENCE): per-row median obd/gps over 2185 paired seconds of 2026-08-06T162657, re-measured 0.915-0.924 on six drives (2026-07-28 to 2026-09-21) by the committee evaluator on 2026-09-25. Every one of those drives was on the pre-HAT USB GNSS receiver, before the 2026-09-23 HAT install, and on the tires as they were then. At ~0.7 Hz in 1 km/h steps it is too coarse to differentiate at the default smoothing and is refused as such by the dyno; listed for completeness of the order. ALSO the trip path's speed correction (M01.2, 2026-11-12): trip distance, average and maximum speed, instant economy and the gear estimate use obd:SPEED / this ratio (src.vehicle.speed_correction). It is a profile constant, deliberately: it drifts as the tires wear (full tread is about 2 % of the rolling radius, so the ECM's reading of true speed moves by up to ~2 % over the tires' life) and the per-drive rolling-circumference estimate (/control/tires) tracks that drift, but the trip path does not follow it yet (M01.2 follow-up). Re-measure after a tire change and record the new value here.

inertia.evidence: ESTIMATES, 2026-09-26, none measured. Wheel side: four road wheels at the profile's measured 40.3 kg per wheel and tire (wheel_tire_assembly_kg) and the 2.559 m rolling circumference (r = 0.407 m; 2.609 m until 2026-10-03, H07.11), with a shape factor of 0.7 of m*r^2 (an LT tire's mass sits near the rim; a solid disc is 0.5, a thin ring 1.0) -- about 19.4 kg m^2. driveline_output_kg_m2 (propshaft, differentials, axle shafts, hubs and rotors, referred to the wheels) is an order-of-magnitude figure, not a part weight. engine_side_kg_m2 (crank, flywheel, clutch, gearbox input) is the PHYSICAL crank-side inertia, a typical 4 L V6 manual figure within a plausible 0.15-0.35 kg m^2. It sits upstream of the driveline losses, so the wheels see eta times it, with eta = 1 - drivetrain_loss_fraction from profiles.yaml (0.85). The one convention is dyno.INERTIA_CONVENTION. H07.6's two-gear pulls measure eta*I_e and replace the estimate (measured_engine). In 3rd (overall 7.11) the estimates add ~119 kg (wheel side) + ~65 kg (0.85 x 0.25 kg m^2 through the ratio) to a ~2,311 kg test mass. A 40 % error in the engine-side estimate therefore moves 3rd-gear wheel force during a pull by ~1.0 %.

AltitudeNoise.description:
GPS altitude noise, measured where the road contributes nothing: parked.

GNSS altitude is not white. On this truck, parked, it wanders by
2.5-5 m (sd) with an autocorrelation still 0.6-0.97 after 20 s
(``~/canary-data/sessions-0920``; ``tests/fixtures/gnss_altitude``), so a
grade standard error that assumes independent samples is 3-10x too small,
and a flat road reads as a crest. From altitude alone, road shape and
receiver wander cannot be told apart at the scale of a segment; a
stationary stretch of the same session measures the wander by itself.

Modelled as white noise plus a powered-exponential wander, with variogram
``γ(h) = white·[h > 0] + correlated·(1 − exp(−(h/τ)^α))``, 0 < α < 2 (a
valid variogram throughout). α = 1 is an AR(1)/Ornstein-Uhlenbeck wander;
real parked altitude here is smoother, γ growing as ~h^1.5 from 1 to 30 s,
which an exponential (linear at short lags) misdescribes at the lags a
segment spans. Every
standard error in :func:`fit_squat` is ``−wᵀ·Γ·w`` for weights ``w`` that
sum to zero (a slope), which needs only the variogram, never the sill, so
a receiver that has not stopped wandering within the reference is still
described at the lags a segment spans.

RoadLoadConditions.description:
What road load depends on: the road, load, tires and air (H07.5).

``baro_kpa`` is required (M01.8): ``C`` is ``½·ρ·Cd·A``, so it belongs to
the air it was fitted in, and a power run at another barometer scales it
by ``ρ_run / ρ_fit`` (:meth:`RoadLoadCoefficients.in_air`). This truck's
roads span 63-82 kPa; a fit at 80 kPa used unscaled at 70 kPa overstates
aero drag by 62 N at 100 km/h. The coast-down sessions' measured
barometer (``obd:BAROMETRIC_PRESSURE`` median over the coasts) is what
goes here; a record without one is refused, never given a default.

copies of the same quantity, so each channel carries its own ratio, as
measured, never a platform default.
